_design_note: M3.3LX. Training is byte-for-byte the m3_3l specification -- same route, features, reward, exploration, task, budget and seeds, still solo -- and only the evaluation suites differ: this arm adds classic_versus_opponents. It exists to fill the one comparison m3_4 cannot make on its own. m3_4 shows what an agent trained against three rule_based opponents scores in the tournament setting, but without this arm there is nothing to say whether training against them helped, because the solo-trained model was never measured there. Re-running the training rather than re-scoring the stored checkpoints keeps the provenance chain intact; the training phase is deterministic and should reproduce m3_3l exactly, which is itself a check.

_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: unknown by design; this is the measurement that decides whether training with opponents is worth its cost, and predicting it would be predicting the answer
_predeclared_design_numbers.purpose: the missing control for m3_4: solo-trained model, tournament evaluation
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: Report all five training-seed distributions and kills, which are structurally possible in this evaluation for the first time on a solo-trained model.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reproduction_check: loot-crate holdout at round 2000 must reproduce m3_3l's 32.622 score exactly; a mismatch means the training phase is not deterministic and every cross-arm comparison in docs/01 section 7 needs re-examination
